events.title: UEFA, other football federations unite against Infantino

events.title: Type 2 diabetes in young women increasingly common

events.title: Germany news: Berlin to step up drone security research
events.summary: Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said Germany is moving to counter the threats posed by drones. Meanwhile, the transport minister said he wants Deutsche Bahn bonuses tied to punctuality targets.

events.title: Study: Obesity 'bigger cancer risk' than previously thought

events.title: FIFA warns against 'concerted effort' to undermine Gianni Infantino
events.summary: Pressure is mounting on the FIFA president Gianni Infantino after plans to sell a stake in the World Cup collapsed and fresh allegations emerged relating to his time at UEFA.

events.title: Germany: Interior Minister warns of 'daily' hybrid warfare
events.summary: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt says attacks by foreign powers have become a constant threat to Germany. His remarks come just days after an explosive-laden drone was found at Leipzig airport.

events.title: When German Catholics and Protestants share a church
events.summary: Each year, dozens of churches are decommissioned, demolished or repurposed in Germany. But there is a new, unique development.

events.title: Germany debates reintroducing mandatory civilian service

events.title: Eco wins: Hungary goes solar, marmots go viral and Rome gets an upgrade
events.summary: From Hungary's accidental solar revolution to marmot crowdfunding and a long-overdue upgrade for Rome's big snake, good news comes in strange packages this week.

events.title: Germany: Far-right AfD extends its lead in nationwide polls
events.summary: In the latest Sunday poll, the AfD continues to pull ahead. And more and more people are against excluding the right-wing populists from decision-making, at least on a case-by-case basis.

events.title: Testosterone and fertility: the trade-off men aren't told about

events.title: Drought threatens power supplies in Danube countries
events.summary: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.

events.title: Mata Hari: Celebrated dancer turns WWI spy

events.title: AfD threatens to cut funding for 'modern-thinking' culture
events.summary: The far-right party could win an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's state election in September. Their cultural program denigrates Bauhaus, Holocaust remembrance culture and diversity in theater.

events.title: How Gianni Infantino rose to rule football

events.title: Why is Russia selling its gold?

events.title: My sleep deprivation is your natural short sleep

events.title: Tennis star Sabalenka supports sport's new sex test policy

events.title: Binging on cringe: It's as addictive as 'eating junk food'

events.title: German court rules that AI music firm Suno violated copyrights

events.title: BMW to Volkswagen: How deep is Germany's auto industry cull?

events.title: Why Germany may stand up against FIFA's World Cup sell-off

events.summary: A Max Planck researcher has developed VR and smartphone tools that let you "meet" your future self. The science behind it is more powerful than it sounds.

events.summary: Young people in much of the world face growing competition for entry-level jobs as graduate numbers rise, hiring slows and AI-driven disruption adds uncertainty to career prospects.

events.title: How heat waves are messing with your sleep
events.summary: Residents across Europe have struggled to sleep during the latest record heat waves. But as the planet continues to warm, sleep deprivation could create an epidemic of mental and physical ill-health.

events.title: England and Liverpool football legend Kevin Keegan dies aged 75
events.summary: English former striker and manager Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75 after a battle with cancer. He was a two-time European footballer of the year with Hamburg.

events.title: How 'blue dot fever' is affecting concerts
events.summary: Live music remains popular, but many concerts are struggling with unsold tickets and cancellations. While superstars fill stadiums, smaller venues and acts are facing a crisis.

events.title: Taking stock of 2026 World Cup: Football's biggest show yet
events.summary: A worthy world champion, a call from the US president, security concerns and a few pleasant surprises: The biggest World Cup ever is now over. So what will we remember about the 2026 World Cup?

events.title: In Ceuta, migrants stranded at Europe’s gates await their fate
events.summary: Weeks after some 70,000 migrants tried to cross from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, the ones who chose to stay have settled on El Trampolin beach. They hail from various countries, speak different languages and crossed many borders to get to this strip of sand. Europe seems very close, and yet so far.

events.title: 'Tons' of nuclear materials found at undisclosed Syrian site, IAEA chief says
events.summary: UN nuclear watchdog head Rafael Grossi said Tuesday that his agency had found several "tons of nuclear materials" at a previously undeclared site dating from the rule of Syria's previous authorities. Syria's Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said the material was not dangerous and that Damascus had the right to keep and use it for peaceful purposes.

events.title: Search launched after sailboat found adrift off French island
events.summary: Search operations were under way Monday evening for anyone who may have been on board a yacht found adrift off a French island. The alert was raised by a passenger aboard a Brittany Ferries vessel travelling from Portsmouth in Britain to Bilbao in Spain, who spotted the yacht apparently in distress.

events.title: Palestinian American challenges Israeli army outside his home in the West Bank
events.summary: For more than a week, militant ​Israeli settlers have encircled Palestinian homes in the West Bank village of Qusra, despite the deployment of the Israeli military. The ongoing siege has prompted Palestinian-American Loui Ridi to come back to his hometown, out of fear that he could lose his property there. On Tuesday he confronted settlers on his land. Story by Emerald Maxwell.

events.title: Sophie Adenot: First French woman to walk in space
events.summary: Sophie Adenot became the first French female astronaut to venture outside the International Space Station for a spacewalk on August 18, accompanied by American astronaut Anil Menon.

events.title: France's Vieira appointed head coach of Senegal national football team
events.summary: Former France midfielder Patrick Vieira has been appointed Senegal coach, succeeding Pape Thiaw following the team's World Cup elimination. Born in Dakar, the 50-year-old takes charge of a national team for the first time after coaching in England, France and Italy. Vieira will begin his tenure next month as Senegal prepares for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

events.title: Volodymyr Zelensky names new Defence minister after weeks of political crisis
events.summary: President ​Volodymyr Zelensky nominated ​Yevheny Khmara for parliamentary approval ​to become Defence minister. Khmara served ​as acting ‌minister following the abrupt dismissal of ‌his predecessor, Mykhailo Fedorov, in June, which ​sparked public outrage and a week-long ​political crisis ​for Zelensky. Details by FRACE 24 correspondent in Kyiv, Emmanuelle Chaze.

events.title: ISS: Sophie Adenot and Anil Menon conduct spacewalk to replace space-to-ground antenna
events.summary: Nadia Massih is pleased to welcome Daniel Neuenschwander, Director of Human and Robotic Exploration at the European Space Agency (ESA). According to Neuenschwander, this latest ISS mission demonstrates what makes the International Space Station exceptional: interdependence. European, American, Japanese, Canadian and Russian partners depend on one another to keep the station functioning, even when relations on Earth are more complicated. Replacing a 90-kilogram communications antenna is a technically demanding task in an environment where every system must function perfectly.

events.title: More and more Christian families pressured to leave the West Bank by Israeli settlers
events.summary: Christian leaders and religious figures in the West Bank say difficult living conditions are pushing an increasing number of Christian families to leave their homes. The reality is threatening the historic presence of Christians in Palestinian territories. France 24's correspondent Majed Saeed reports.

Gang leader masterminded Tupac's killing, prosecutor tells jury

events.title: 🔴 Middle East live: US says Israel behind strikes on military airport in Syria
Singapore’s seniors turn to parkour to boost balance and strength
events.summary: Parkour may conjure images of rowdy teenagers swinging from building to building in urban landscapes, but since 2017, coach Tan Shie Boon has been using these techniques to improve Singaporean seniors’ strength and agility. Tan’s Movement Singapore classes have gone viral online, showing people in their 60s and 70s climbing structures, vaulting over railings, rolling down slanted surfaces and jumping off platforms.

events.title: Ebola in DRC: Deadliest outbreak on record ‘outpacing the response’
events.summary: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome WHO Spokesperson Tarik Jašarević. His central concern is that we do not yet know where all the places the Ebola virus is circulating: infected people remain outside treatment centres, transmission chains go undetected, and patients who seek care too late face much poorer chances of survival. Conflict, population mobility and other humanitarian pressures make surveillance more difficult, but community engagement is equally crucial. Without trust and cooperation, testing, contact tracing, safe burials and early treatment cannot work effectively.

events.title: Heatwaves damage Monet's gardens in the North of France
events.summary: The succession of heatwaves in France this year has played havoc with plants and husbandry, including in Claude Monet's celebrated home and gardens at Giverny, in Normandy. Some of the garden's most famous attractions have been damaged by the heat, as our colleagues at France 2 and Oliver Farry explain.

events.title: Is Meta deliberately making children addicted to its social media platforms?
events.summary: Social media giant Meta, is set to defend itself in a landmark trial. They are accused of knowingly and deliberately designing features which get children under the age of 13 addicted to its platforms. Story by Delano D'Souza.

events.title: West Bank village of Qusra under siege by extremist Israeli settlers
events.summary: In the occupied West Bank, the Palestinian village of Qusra remains under siege by extremist Israeli settlers. They are trying to force families off their land through tactics including cutting off access to food and water. A Palestinian-American who owns a house in the village has returned to Qusra from Ohio. Louai Abo Ridi says he fears for safety amid reports of the Israeli army turning a blind eye to settler violence. In this clip from today, you get a sense of the tensions between him and the soldiers. Analysis by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor, Philip Turle.

events.title: At least 20 elephants died in Kenya, theory of cyanide poisoning contested
events.summary: In Kenya, wildlife experts are pushing back over the theory that blames 20 mysterious elephant deaths on cyanide poisoning from pesticides used on nearby farmland. Laurent Berstecher explains.

events.title: ‘Come fetch your people’: 300 anti-migrants protesters call out to SADC leaders
events.summary: South Africa hosted a gathering of leaders from the southern African regional bloc amid xenophobic violence and anti-migrant protests. As the continent’s wealthiest country, South Africa has long attracted migrants, but it faces an unemployment rate of over 30 percent and deep-seated inequalities. Pretoria has called for a continent-wide conference on the issue of migration. Details by Eunice Masson, FRANCE 24 correspondent in Cape Town.

events.title: Astronaut Sophie Adenot will be first French woman to walk in space
events.summary: This French woman is making history. Sophie Adenot is set to become the first French woman to complete a space walk this Tuesday, when she conducts repairs to the outside of the ISS. She'll spend around 6h30 on the task, which is very physically demanding. Details by Ellen Gainsford.

events.title: Somali army repels troops loyal to ousted leader and Islamist insurgents
events.summary: Somali national forces repelled an assault by troops loyal to an ousted regional leader and Islamist insurgents on Monday over control of the key city of Baidoa. events.title: French PM announces support for fire-damaged villages after jeers from residents
events.summary: The French government has approved a special budget worth 12 million euros to help towns affected by the recent wildfires in the country's south. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced a raft of other support measures including tax breaks for companies affected by the calamity. Earlier, he was jeered by some inhabitants when he visited Le Porge where 183 homes were ravaged by fire. Story by Yuka Royer.

events.title: Trump threatens to bomb Oman, as its ally tires to mediate Iran negotiations
events.summary: As the 60-day ceasefire deadline passes, US President Donald Trump is lashing out at an American ally trying to mediate negotiations between the US and Iran. Using an expletive, Trump threatened to bomb Oman if it "gets in the way." This isn’t the first time Trump has threatened Oman. Details by Monte Francis.

events.title: In Jerusalem, US negotiator Jared Kushner presses Netanyahu about Gaza deal
events.summary: Mideast negotiator and Trump son-in-law Jared Kushner was meeting Monday with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, days after the premier rejected the US-backed road map to move the ceasefire deal forward in Gaza. events.title: Jason Arday, ex-Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism, found dead a week after resigning
events.summary: Former Cambridge professor Jason Arday was found dead at his London home on Friday, one week after he resigned from his position after accusations of plagiarism.

events.title: Magnitude-7.7 quake hits off coast of Indonesia, killing at least 47
events.summary: A magnitude-7.7 earthquake hit off the coast of Indonesia in the eastern Flores region, the United States Geological Survey reported on Friday.
